comments.text:
Hmmm normally I like your reviews and while I understand everyone has their preferences, this review does feel nitpicky (in fact it feels like a bad review) 

E.g. It's kinda expected to have those black bars when watching videos on a phone. It's like complaining the pen in S Ultra is too thin for a regular grip 

I'm sure people who bought a phone knew that they were going to expect those black bars if their screen is not the same as the aspect ratio of the video. Even the Ultra you showed, had black bars. 

And versatility is very important to many people. A smartphone is pretty much the epitome of versatility. Not many would want to carry a non-smart phone, a DSLR, a flashlight, a calculator, a map, a calendar, a compass just because on their own they would be specialized products, great or even perfect at what they do.

A 2-in-1 solves issues for many people, its versatility at being either a laptop or a tablet at anytime while being more portable  is likely why some people go for it. Pretty unrealistic if people want to start wishing it was the perfect laptop and the perfect tablet at the same time

A review about how a versatile phone is not the perfect slab phone nor the perfect mini tablet. But you did not say how it was not as good as the Ultra it was compared to, nor how it was not good as a mini tablet (except being unable to write with a S Pen)

comments.text:
Definitely tricky to open. But I worry more about closing, as it requires to push lightly on the screen. However, it means it closes tightly and I'd be very confident that it won't let dirt in. I think it's worth that trade off.

A case will make it easier to open. And eliminate the wobble (otherwise leave it screen down when not in use). 

I thought I would be more flip than fold, but trying out the flip7 I quickly realised I would rarely use it folded. Just too fiddly, apart from the odd widget. So it would be closed only when not in use, and opened up and closed a lot. Which raises durability questions. And the softer screen for daily phone like interacts, felt a step back. I really felt very meh about a product I had seriously been considering.  

The fold7 however, I had rejected for price and YouTubers regularly questioning how useful the tablet mode is. And the opposite happened, I tried it and was floored. I couldn't pick from all the other phones, but this instantly wowed me. Not just the goldilocks between s25+ (good width) and ultra (build, cameras), but attractive especially in blue, no ugly Chinese or Google Cyclops phone module even if the one on board has its own disadvantages. For me, I'm sure I will be 90% phone mode. I have an old 10" tablet I've been thinking about upgrading but didn't as I couldn't justify the cost for an occasional use device. This fixes that problem. I can leave the work iPad at home when travelling. Emails I could always check on my 6' screen, but attachments were annoying, spreadsheets a pain and forget calling someone while viewing docs. 

I get why people that review phones and tech from a tech perspective reject these. If you just view it as a bigger screen for media and games, I think you miss the point and money could be better spent elsewhere. 

For me, as a tool for everyday, family but also work it is convenience and productivity heaven. I really wanted a Microsoft duo when I couldn't afford or justify one. This for me is the evolution of that.

Typing this on my fold 7 now, upgrading from the fold 5 and I loved that phone. The crease was making a bit of noise and the battery had lost capacity so when Samsung offered $900 trade in plus other incentives and discounts I jumped on the train. The biggest things I've noticed is weight and thickness loss makes a huge difference in the pocket and when holding your phone for a long time. I am really bothered by the hole punch on the inner display and disappointed to see no spen support. At this point if they made an spen that was entirely self contained without needing the extra display layers I'd get that. 

Other then that, what I have really also enjoyed is the standard 21:9 exterior display. The fold 5 was always narrow and while I for used to it, typing never felt right and watching 16:9 videos on it was terrible. Now I find myself using the exterior display more and the inner display less. But I think it's betters this way. I also am now holding the phone open in portrait orientation watching videos full screen, instead of landscape. It's slightly smaller viewing frame this way but at least no annoying cutout to stare at.

Having waited for six generations, I am delighted to have acquired the Z Fold 6, and I am pleased with my purchase.

My intention was not to use it for watching movies, but rather for productivity. Having used it for a year, I have thoroughly enjoyed it.

Interestingly, the outer screen, which some considered a significant drawback in the Z Fold 6 due to its size compared to a standard screen, has become my favorite feature. This is because it allows me to use the phone with one hand, and I find myself using it for approximately 60% of the time.

The remaining 40% is spent on the large inner screen, where I engage in various activities:
- I simultaneously use three apps: browser, email, and either WhatsApp or documents (PDFs, Word, Excel).
- I review VMs logs and can easily scale services when I am away from my laptop.
- I read documents and books (Kindle) while on the move.
- I take notes during meetings and brainstorm ideas, thanks to the S-Pen, which was a key factor in choosing the Z Fold over other foldable devices.
- I play games, and it is incredibly enjoyable on the large screen. You will certainly appreciate it.

I was fond of the Z-Fold 7's design and was considering an upgrade until I learned that it does not support the S-Pen.

I sincerely hope that Samsung will release a model with S-Pen support, as we value it and would not want to see it discontinued.

If not Samsung, then perhaps other manufacturers will consider this feature.

I bought my fold 7 a few days ago and here's what i think coming from a S22 plus after years of using Samsung slab style phones.
I never want to go back to a slab style phone again, one of the biggest issues i've had with those kind of phones is the fact that the screen real estate is just not enough for me, having to scroll side to side in many cases just to check something out becomes so bothersome. I hoped that feeling would go away but nope.
- I've had the S2, S3, S5, Note 4, S6 Edge, S7, S9, S10, S20+ S22, none of them ever felt like they had enough screen real estate.

- I agree it's hard to open, today i'm going to get a case and then i'll see if that makes a difference, i think it will and it'll negate the hard to open argument instantly as there's more to grip. Sure some people don't like cases but when a phone is this expensive? damn sure i'm going to use a case. I also did on every S line iteration i'v owned since the S6 basically.
- I do agree there should have been something to get some grip on it to open it more easily, like a knurled texture the size of the volume buttons for example.

- S-pen? useless for me personally and when there's not enough people using it I can see why they got rid of it.

- Selfie camera ugh I wish it wasn't there to begin with, under display version was even uglier in my opinion. As for the bump on the back from the cameras, for me it's a moot point as i'm putting on a case anyway and probably a ring on the back just so it's more secure in my hands and at same time negates the wobble if i ever want to use it sat on a flat surface.

- I could care less about multitasking, one of the biggest things I love about it is the fact that i get so much more screen estate when I want to, when i'm sitting down I can get a big screen experience instantly and when i'm on the move the outer screen is just like using a slab style smartphone.

- The crease was one of my biggest gripes with the previous Fold iterations, I still don't like it but honestly having only used my Fold 7 a few hours so far since i've gotten it, It's something I notice I accepted as it's far less obtrusive then it was before.
I highly highly doubt the crease will be gone entirely next year, based off of how foldables have progressed I think it'll be over 4 generations more before that crease is entirely gone.

So far i'm still in testing out phase and yeah one big issue I haven't mentioned above is the black bars on top and bottom of youtube videos but i'll make up my mind once i've used this phone more. If I return my Fold 7 i'd use my S22 plus again for the time being but I definitely won't be buying a new slab style phone again that's for sure.

PS: I haven't watched one of your videos in years and now I'm reminded again why. I respect you have your opinion but as others have pointed out this is nitpicking.
